articles.title: Return policy
articles.body: Unused items in original condition can be returned within 60 days of delivery for a full refund. Used gear can be returned within 30 days if it has a defect. Clearance items and opened fuel canisters are final sale.

articles.body: To start a return, open the Orders page, choose the order, and select Return Items. Print the prepaid shipping label and drop the package at any carrier location, or bring the item to any Timberwick Outfitters store.

articles.title: Tent and shelter warranty
articles.body: Timberwick tents and shelters have a 2-year warranty against defects in materials and workmanship, including broken poles, failed seams, and broken zippers. Damage from wear, fire, or animals is not covered. Send a photo of the problem with your order number to start a warranty claim.

articles.title: Choosing a sleeping bag temperature rating
articles.body: Sleeping bag ratings list a comfort temperature and a lower limit. Pick a bag whose comfort rating is at least 10 degrees colder than the coldest night you expect. Down bags pack smaller, while synthetic bags stay warmer when wet.

articles.title: Backpack sizing
articles.body: Backpacks are sized by torso length, not height. Measure from the bony bump at the base of your neck to the top of your hip bones. Small fits 15 to 17 inches, medium fits 17 to 19 inches, and large fits 19 to 21 inches.

articles.title: Hiking boot sizing and break-in
articles.body: Try boots on in the afternoon with the socks you plan to hike in. Leave about a finger's width of space at the toe. Break in new boots on short walks for one to two weeks before a long trip.

articles.title: Shipping restrictions for stove fuel
articles.body: Stove fuel canisters and other hazardous materials can only ship by ground to addresses in the lower 48 states. They cannot ship by air, to PO boxes, or internationally. You can also buy fuel in any store.
